title: The Pose It Cannot Reach Slowly: Singularities and What They Cost

questions.question: A 0.5 and 0.4 metre arm is asked to move its tool outward at 0.1 m/s. At half reach the elbow turns at 0.27 rad/s. What does it need a tenth of a millimetre from full extension?
options: 15 rad/s, about 140 revolutions a minute, and ten times that again a tenth of the distance closer
About 0.5 rad/s, a little more
Nothing: the tool cannot move at all
About 2 rad/s
questions.explanation: The determinant of this arm's Jacobian is l1 l2 sin(q2) exactly, so it depends on the elbow and nothing else and is zero with the arm straight. The rate goes up as the determinant goes down.

questions.question: At exactly full extension, what can the tool do?
options: Move sideways but not outward, at any joint speed: the arm has lost a direction
Nothing at all
Everything, but slowly
Move outward only, since the arm is aligned with that direction
questions.explanation: That is what a singularity is. It is not that the numbers get large, it is that one direction becomes unreachable, and approaching it the cost of moving that way grows without bound.

questions.question: The elbow up and elbow down solutions are 3.96 radians apart at half reach. How far apart are they a hundredth of a millimetre from full extension?
options: 0.019 radians, so which one a solver picks is decided by a rounding error
Still about 4 radians: the postures are always distinct
Exactly zero, so the solver reports a failure
About 0.5 radians
questions.explanation: Both answers remain exactly correct, so nothing in the solver has anything to complain about, and the arm swings through half its workspace to satisfy a request that moved the tool by a millimetre.

questions.question: Damped least squares is added, with lambda 0.01, at that near-singular pose. What happens to the requested 0.1 m/s?
options: It delivers 0.027 m/s at a quarter of the joint rate: damping costs speed and rate together
It delivers 0.1 m/s with bounded joint rates
It delivers 0.1 m/s but in the wrong direction
It refuses, since the matrix is still singular
questions.explanation: The matrix inverted is J J' + lambda squared I, which cannot be singular, so there is always an answer. The answer is not the motion you asked for, and that is the correct behaviour.

questions.question: Should damping be switched on only near singularities?
options: No: at half reach with lambda 0.01 the tool still moves at over 99 percent of the speed asked, so leaving it on removes a mode
Yes, it costs too much elsewhere
Yes, otherwise the arm never reaches full speed
It makes no difference either way
questions.explanation: What does need reporting is the shortfall: J q against v is the number that tells a path follower it is falling behind rather than tracking.

questions.question: The tool is falling behind near full extension because of damping. What should slow down?
options: The whole path in time, since slowing one direction and not the others distorts the shape being drawn
Only the direction that is limited
The joint that is turning fastest
Nothing: the follower should accept the error
questions.explanation: A time scaling preserves the shape, and it is what a trajectory generator does with this information. Choose lambda from the joint rate you can afford, which is on the arm's data sheet, rather than by feel.
